simple.meaning: שְׁכַח (shᵉkach) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to discover (literally or figuratively).” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 18 times across Ezra, Daniel, beginning at Ezra 4:15. Its contexts include family, offering, kingship, priesthood, city, mountain.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to שְׁכַח (H7912).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.

definitions.full: H7912. shekach [ שְׁכַח ] verb Haph`el (K § 40, 4 Nö GGA 1884, 1019 ) find ( שְׁכַח ᵑ7 find , Syriac , Christian-Palestinian Aramaic Schulth Lex. 205 ; Egyptian Aramaic השכח S-C E 5, pass. אשתכךְ RŠS 361A 2 ): — Perfect 1singular הַשְׁכַּ֫חַת Dan 2:25 ; 3 masculine plural הַשְׁכַּ֫חוּ Ezra 4:19 ; Dan 6:12 ; Imperfect 2masculine singular תְּהַשְׁכַּת Ezra 4:15 ; 7:16 ; Infinitive לְהַשְׁכָּחָה Dan 6:5 (twice in verse); — find , accusative of thing, 6:5 ( ל person), 6:5 ; 6:6 ( ל person), 6:6 ( עַל person, accusative of thing omitted), Ezra 7:16 ( ב location); followed by clause דִּי 4:15 ( ב location), 4:19 ; accusative of person Dan 2:25 ; ל person 6:12 ( + participle action.). Hithpe`el Perfect 3masculine singular הִשְׁתְּכַח Dan 2:35 +, 2 masculine singular כַ֫חַתְּ - 5:27 , 3 feminine singular כַ֫חַת - 5:11 +; be found , subject thing, ב location, Ezra 6:2 ; ב person Dan 5:11-12 , 14 ; 6:24 ; עַל person 6:5 ; ל person + קֳדָם person 6:23 ; ל of thing 2:35 (see אֲתַר ); subject person 5:27 + חַסִּר thou hast been found wanting (K § 85, 3 ). שַׁכְלְלֵהּ etc., see כלל .
definitions.rootNote: (Aramaic) corresponding to 7911 through the idea of disclosure of a covered or forgotten thing;
